name: Bukharinism
summary: Bukharinism is the programme of Nikolai Bukharin and the Right Opposition in the mid-1920s Soviet Union: keep the New Economic Policy, build socialism gradually through a mixed economy of state industry, cooperatives and peasant farming, and hold the worker-peasant alliance together under party leadership. It keeps the Bolshevik framework of proletarian dictatorship, a ruling party and world revolution, but rejects forced requisition and forced collectivisation.
scope: The mature Bukharin of 1921-1929 (NEP, the smychka, the dispute with the Left Opposition and with Stalin's turn), taken from his Economic Structure of Soviet Russia (1922), Draft Comintern Programme (1922), Historical Materialism (1921), Tasks of the Russian Communist Party (1926), World Revolution and the USSR (1927) and Notes of an Economist (1928). Excludes the ultra-left War Communism of 1918-20, the jointly written 1919 ABC of Communism as a source, Stalin-era trial confessions and later market-socialist reformers' use of his name.

sources.usedFor: Bukharin's statement of Marxist social theory: class struggle, the state, the productive forces.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The programme calls for arming the proletariat, organising disciplined armed forces and rejects pacifism as a principle.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: The draft programme subordinates all large banks to a Central State Bank, not leaving money to the market.

abolish-ip.rationale: The programme lists the absence of patent rights among the features of communist society but he does not discuss them for the transition.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The programme headlines the inevitable breakdown of the capitalist system and describes post-war capitalism as absolutely unstable.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: The programme calls wars as inevitable an accompaniment of capitalism as crises and unemployment, and traces 1914 to the rivalry over colonies.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: The programme says capitalism's drive for profit developed the productive forces and created the concentration, technique and science that are the premises of socialism.

central-planning.rationale: The draft programme sets a rational plan against competitive anarchy, and Bean reports planning as his ultimate goal, though he wanted plan and market to complement each other in the NEP years.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: He backs colonial movements against imperialism and the right of separation for former colonies, which rules out rule over them for their own improvement.

class-collaboration.rationale: The programme calls the class war an inherent feature of capitalism and demands the proletariat's dictatorship, and the 1926 speech expects class struggle inside the cooperatives.

class-struggle-history.rationale: His textbook cites the maxim that the struggle between classes is the motive force of history, and the programme calls capitalist society's whole history one of class conflict.

collective-farming.rationale: He saw cooperatives and, later, collective and state farms as the long-term road for agriculture, but by persuasion; Bean records his opposition to forced collectivisation.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The draft programme demands the liberation of the colonies and calls their exploitation the central point of capitalist oppression.

corporate-influence.rationale: The programme says the bourgeoisie secures its economic domination by political rule and state organisation, with finance capital holding state power.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: He describes the Italian corporative state as a form of state capitalism and a special type of state power.

defeat-communism.rationale: Communism is the final aim of the programme, and it expects the proletarian and capitalist systems to coexist only temporarily through compromises.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: The programme condemns the Social Democrats for backing their own imperialist governments in 1914, but says the question of defending one's country can no longer be put so generally.

democracy-best.rationale: He set the soviet dictatorship of the proletariat against bourgeois democracy, which he called a veiled dictatorship, and held that exploiters must be suppressed.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: He held that free competitive elections under capitalism give only formal rights, and judged a state democratic by whose class it serves.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: The programme calls the proletarian dictatorship the unavoidable premise for the transition to communism, and the 1927 article praises the USSR as that dictatorship.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The programme promises equality of all citizens whatever their sex, race or religion, yet gives the proletariat legal privileges and suppresses the exploiters.

equal-outcomes.rationale: The programme says every difference between poverty and wealth disappears in communist society, though wage differences remain in the transition.

farm-price-support.rationale: He wanted cooperatives to give peasants cheaper credit, purchasing and marketing, and Bean reports he pressed for higher grain prices to keep farmers producing.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: A programme that makes the right of separation binding rules out using force to stop peoples from leaving.

free-trade.rationale: His programme includes a state monopoly of foreign trade, and he warned against dependence on foreign markets controlled by capitalism.

gradual-change.rationale: Bean reports his gradualism in economic policy, which sits beside a programme of revolutionary overthrow.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Abolishing private ownership of the means of production ends exploitation, so that work is no longer done for others' profit, in the draft programme's account.

independent-unions.rationale: The draft programme says unions must be organs of the proletarian power under the party's leadership.

land-redistribution.rationale: He treated the break-up of the landed estates and the transfer of land to the peasants as the achievement of the first half of the revolution, and the draft programme nationalises large estates and hands part to the peasantry.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: The core of Bukharinism: a mixed market economy with state industry on the commanding heights under proletarian power, which he defended as the road to socialism.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Bukharin used markets as the road into socialism but treated spontaneity as the feature of the transition economy that planning must overcome.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: The textbook holds that the form of society is determined by the development of the productive forces and that ideologies rest on an economic basis.

moral-incentives.rationale: The draft programme holds that individual material stimulation is necessary for the transitional period, not to be replaced by moral incentives.

nation-first.rationale: His programme subordinates local and national interests of the movement to the international one and treats the revolution as a world process.

national-self-determination.rationale: The draft programme makes the right of peoples to self-determination, including complete separation, binding on bourgeois and proletarian states.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Communism is the final aim of the programme and capitalism's breakdown is held inevitable, leaving no third course.

night-watchman-state.rationale: He gave the state ownership of the commanding heights of industry, banking and transport, far beyond defence and justice.

no-central-bank.rationale: The draft programme centralises the banks under a Central State Bank after the revolution.

no-transition-to-communism.rationale: The programme describes a long transition period between capitalism and communism, which he took to be the main business of the Soviet state.

one-party-rule.rationale: The programme says the proletariat succeeds only when the party has the leadership, and Bean reports his remark that in the USSR one party was in power and the others in prison.

parliamentary-road-socialism.rationale: The programme holds that revolutionary overthrow of the bourgeois state is the premise of communism and that bourgeois democracy is a veiled dictatorship.

party-controls-media.rationale: The programme lists monopolising the most important printing establishments and newspapers among the proletarian state's first measures.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: The programme demands unqualified execution of the resolutions of the leading organs and discipline in the ranks of the Communist parties.

party-own-road.rationale: The programme requires international Communist discipline with unqualified execution of the Comintern's resolutions by each national section.

pay-for-effort.rationale: The draft programme says piece work, bonus systems and individual stimulation to work are unavoidably necessary during the transition.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: The programme argues that formal democratic rights are fiction while capital monopolises the means of production, and that only the soviet state secures workers' press liberty.

production-for-use.rationale: The programme says communist society ends profit-making for personal benefit, though NEP state enterprises still produced for the market.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The draft programme describes the working class as the living source of profit for the bourgeoisie that exploits its labour, and the 1922 essay speaks of the surplus value capitalists take.

promote-democracy-abroad.rationale: The programme calls bourgeois democracy a veiled form of bourgeois dictatorship, so promoting it abroad runs against his stated view.

property-fundamental.rationale: The draft programme proposes expropriating large property without compensation as a first measure of the proletarian state.

public-ownership.rationale: The draft programme calls for expropriating large industry, transport and electric works, and the 1922 essay treats the nationalised enterprises as owned by the workers' state.

recall-officials.rationale: The programme lists the right to elect new delegates and the right to recall them among the marks of proletarian democracy.

religion-illusion.rationale: The programme says the new culture will bury religion and mysticism for all time and counts the return to religion among the signs of bourgeois decay.

right-to-secede.rationale: The programme states the right of complete separation from the state, under bourgeois and proletarian rule alike.

separated-powers.rationale: The programme names the combination of executive and legislative power as a mark of soviet democracy against the bourgeois parliamentary republic.

smash-state-machine.rationale: The programme says seizure of power is the destruction of the bourgeois state apparatus by the fighting organs of the proletariat.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: He judged the Soviet economy socialist because the working class owned it through its state, so the ownership forms follow from workers' power.

socialism-one-country.rationale: He rejected the view that socialism cannot be built in one country alone and held that building it was possible, though exposed to danger from abroad.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The 1926 speech argues against the view that Soviet state industry is state-capitalist, and the 1922 essay says workers' state enterprises must not be so designated.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Bukharin calls the state the monopolist organisation of the ruling class and the organisation of the ruling class in his textbook of Marxist sociology.

state-directs-investment.rationale: He defended state-led industrialisation, with the planning commission setting export, import and production programmes and resources steered to industry.

state-harmful.rationale: The programme calls the dictatorship of the proletariat the elementary premise of social evolution and holds the state withers only as classes disappear.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The programme has the proletarian state take over all schools and puts the fight against religion first among the fights against prejudice, to be waged with tact.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The programme has counter-revolutionary action suppressed rigorously, and Bean reports his acceptance of a one-party state with other parties in prison.

taxation-theft.rationale: Bean reports he called for heavier taxation and regulation of the private traders to finance industry, treating taxation as legitimate state action.

unions-good.rationale: The 1922 essay assigns unions a role in every sector, from organising state factories to strikes in private enterprises, and the programme treats them as organs of workers' power.

vanguard-party.rationale: The programme says the dictatorship needs a united, disciplined, centralised party that plays the leading role, and the proletariat is led as vanguard by it.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Bean reports his view that large-scale production ultimately drives out small-scale production, and he aimed to turn peasants towards cooperatives under state industry.

women-suffrage.rationale: The programme says proletarian democracy realises equality of all citizens without difference of sex, race, religion or nationality.

worker-farmer-alliance.rationale: The 1926 speech makes the link between the working class and the middle peasantry the first object of policy, and Bean calls the alliance the NEP's long-term policy.

workers-councils.rationale: The programme holds the soviet form best adapted to proletarian power and sets it against the bourgeois parliamentary republic.

workers-nation.rationale: The programme organises workers in the Communist International under international discipline, and the 1927 article treats world revolution as one process.

workers-own-party.rationale: He treats the Communist parties as the workers' own mass parties, separate from the Social Democrats, whom the programme calls a counter-revolutionary force.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: The programme describes the colonies as objects of plunder and the weaker states as dependent on the great powers, though it does not put poverty's cause in these terms.

missingStatements.text: Farmers should not be forced into collective farms.
missingStatements.rationale: Bukharin contrasted the iron broom of forced requisition under War Communism with leading peasants by their own interests, and the draft programme says to put no barriers in the way of the peasantry's individual motives.

quotes.text: instead of driving the peasant forcibly into Communism, he is led by his own private capitalistic interests, gradually, and unnoticed by himself, to Communism
quotes.where: The new economic policy paragraph, beginning 'Formerly, we tried to drive the peasants into Communism'

quotes.text: set up no barriers to the individualistic working motives of the peasantry
quotes.where: Section III.C, last paragraphs on the transition from capitalism to socialism

notes: Searched all statement themes against the six full texts. Answers rest mainly on Bukharin's own 1921-28 writings and his Comintern draft programme (a document of the International, drafted by him); the NEP-era economic answers are the school's distinctive core. Themes with no recorded position (ecology, technology, most of society and culture, immigration, policing, most government mechanics) are null. Bean's article is critical of NEP; only its historical exposition is used. The 1928 Notes of an Economist is read in a German translation. Bukharin's pre-1921 positions (ABC of Communism, 1918 ultra-left works) are not used.

keyFigures.role: Chief theorist and defender of the NEP and leader of the Right Opposition
